It's not just you: Google Maps traffic lines have disappeared for many users

2026-07-27 Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority Google Maps, traffic lines, bug, color-coded traffic, navigation, Android, iOS, desktop
Read the source article

Quick summary

A server-side Google Maps bug caused color-coded traffic lines (green, yellow, orange, red) to vanish from the map interface across Android, iOS, and desktop, leaving commuters without visual traffic density indicators until Google deployed a fix.

Key takeaways

  • A Google Maps bug completely removed color-coded traffic lines from the map overview while underlying traffic data, road closures, and route calculations remained functional
  • The issue affected Android, iOS, and desktop web browsers simultaneously, suggesting a server-side rather than client-side problem
  • Standard troubleshooting steps—toggling traffic layers, clearing cache, switching accounts—did not resolve the issue
  • Reddit user Czerwony150 first flagged the issue, noting that traffic colors "suddenly stopped working out of nowhere"
  • Google confirmed a fix was available by July 28, though full restoration took several hours to reach all users
